summary: FidelityManager's explicit registry bound is caller-configurable but has no project-owned upper ceiling or safe-integer limit. validateConfig accepts any positive finite integer for maxRegisteredEntities, so a configuration can legally disable the practical memory bound that the manager and Reality-Grade architecture rely on.
evidence: At retained production head 827ce0cf63ca5f322502de883beb9f43581c69f2, DEFAULT_CONFIG.maxRegisteredEntities is 4096, but validateConfig only requires maxRegisteredEntities >= 1, finite, and equal to math.floor(value). It does not require <= 2^53-1 or any project-owned operational maximum.

Values such as 1e308 satisfy the current positive/finite/integer test in Luau while making capacity rejection unreachable in any realistic process lifetime. The _states table can therefore grow until external memory/process limits rather than a meaningful FidelityManager budget.

The focused suite proves capacity rejection only with maxRegisteredEntities = 1 and labels the behavior 'registered state is hard bounded'; there is no acceptance-at-maximum/rejection-over-maximum regression for the configuration itself.

This is separate from the retained rejected-step atomicity, plain-input, numeric-operator, registration-order, callback reentrancy, cross-entity transaction, and metrics-accounting hardening in the #385/#398 lineage.
Repository PR/issue search found no existing FidelityManager maxRegisteredEntities capacity-ceiling or safe-integer finding/repair.

UNRENDERED's Reality-Grade performance architecture requires costly subsystem state/caches/queues to have configurable but real project-owned resource budgets; a caller-selected finite integer with no ceiling does not provide such a bound.
Static GitHub source/test/history review only. This worker did not run the test suite or Roblox Studio and makes no runtime-memory measurement claim.
recommendedAction: Create a bounded FidelityManager resource-contract successor when the scheduler permits it. Define an explicit project-owned maximum registration capacity that is both a safe integer and operationally meaningful, reject maxRegisteredEntities above that limit before manager construction, and add exact boundary/max+1 regressions while preserving the existing default 4096 and capacity-rejection metric semantics. Keep the threshold configurable below the project maximum rather than hard-coding all managers to one size.
